questions.question: What are stable equilibrium and unstable equilibrium positions? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• What are stable equilibrium and unstable equilibrium positions? [K]/[CO4]
  • Ans. A body is in stable equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it experiences a
  • restoring force or torque that brings it back to its original position. In potential energy
  • curve it is the minimum energy position.
  • Example: A ball resting at the bottom of a bowl. If nudged, it rolls back to the bottom.
  • A body is in unstable equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it experiences a force or
  • torque that moves it further away from its original position. In potential energy curve
  • it is the maximum energy position.
  • Example: A ball balanced at the top of a hill. If nudged, it rolls down and never returns
  • to the top.

questions.question: Define projectile motion. What are the assumptions made in the study of projectile motion? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Define projectile motion. What are the assumptions made in the study of projectile
  • motion? [K]/[CO3]
  • Ans. A projectile is a body that is given an initial velocity and then follows a path
  • determined entirely by the effects of gravitational acceleration and air resistance. To
  • analyse the motion of a projectile, we represent the projectile as a particle with an
  • acceleration (due to gravity) that is constant in both magnitude and direction. We’ll
  • ignore the effects of air resistance and the curvature and rotation of the earth. Projectile
  • motion is always confined to a vertical plane determined by the direction of the initial
  • velocity- i.e. projectile motion is two-dimensional. Projectile motion can be analysed
  • as a combination of horizontal motion with constant velocity and vertical motion with
  • constant acceleration.

questions.question: An iceboat is at rest on a frictionless horizontal surface. Due to the blowing wind, 4.0 s after the iceboat is released, it is moving to the right at 6.0 m/s (about 22 km/h, or 13 mi/h). What constant horizontal force does the wind exert on the iceboat?

  • after the iceboat is released, it is moving to the right at 6.0m/s(about 22 km/h, or 13
  • mi/h). What constant horizontal force does the wind exert on the iceboat? CO-3, LD-A
  • Ans. Mass of the object is not given in this question, so let as take it as “M".
  • F = ma 2 marks

  • Where: Final velocity v = 6.0m/s. Initial velocity u = 0m/s. Time interval t = 4.0s.
  • The average acceleration aav g = v−ut = 6.0m/s −04.0s = 6.04.0 = 1.5m/s2 2 marks

questions.question: Derive the expression for terminal speed in a fluid medium. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Derive the expression for terminal speed in a fluid medium. [U]/[CO3]
  • Ans. Because of the effects of fluid resistance, an object falling in a fluid does not have
  • a constant acceleration. Let 𝑚 be the mass of a small ball moving through a fluid. Using
  • Newton’s second law,
  • Σ𝐹 = 𝑚𝑔 + ൫−𝑘𝑣௬൯ = 𝑚𝑎௬
  • When the ball first starts to move, 𝑣௬ = 0, the resisting force is zero and the initial
  • acceleration is 𝑎௬ = g. As the speed increases, the resisting force also increases, until
  • finally it is equal in magnitude to the weight. At this time
  • mg - k𝑣௬ = 0,
  • the acceleration is zero, and there is no further increase in speed.
  • The final speed 𝑣௧ , called the terminal speed, is given by
  • mg - k𝑣௧ = 0, or 𝑣௧ =
